::: {.lead}
Today an AI assistant helps you start a short talk, and you check and
finish it in PowerPoint. Each experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in the
AI assistant and PowerPoint on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with PowerPoint, a browser and an AI
  assistant that the university allows (for example
  `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with PowerPoint.
- **The topic:** *Healthy habits in the exam weeks*, a talk for your
  classmates. Use no personal data of other people.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · From an AI outline to slides

**The idea:** ask an AI tool for an **outline**, not for finished slides. A
good outline prompt has five parts: the **topic**, the **audience**, the
**length** (4 slides, 3 minutes), the **form** (a title and 3 points per
slide) and a **limit** (at most 8 words per point); add "Do not invent
numbers or sources." In PowerPoint, **View › Outline**: a line at the left
edge is a new slide, **Tab** makes a line a point, **Shift + Tab** makes it
a title again.

**Aim:** turn an AI outline into slides with Outline view.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Send this prompt: *Make an outline of 4 slides for a 3-minute talk to my
   classmates about healthy habits in the exam weeks. Each slide: a title
   and 3 points, at most 8 words per point. Do not invent numbers or
   sources.* Read the outline.

   {{< record "The title of slide 2 … ; a point that is too long (or: none)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good outline has 4 titles (for example *Sleep well*, *Eat and drink
   well*, *Take short breaks*, *Move every day*) with 3 short points each.
   Shorten every point with more than 8 words.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which part of the prompt is each phrase? Sort them.

   The audience
   :   to my classmates

       Why: Who listens to the talk.

   The length
   :   4 slides for a 3-minute talk

       Why: How long the talk is.

   The form
   :   Each slide: a title and 3 points

       Why: How each slide looks.

   The limit
   :   at most 8 words per point

       Why: A limit that keeps the slides short.
   :::

2. Copy the outline. In a new presentation, open **View › Outline** and
   paste it. Use **Tab** and **Shift + Tab** until every title is a slide
   and every point is under its title. Choose a theme.

   {{< record "Slides in the outline: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **4 slides**, each with its title and 3 points (plus a title slide if
   you add one). A line at the left edge is a slide title; Tab moves a line
   right and makes it a point.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Outline view, a point *Sleep 8 hours a night* is at the left edge, so
   it became a new slide. What do you press?

   - [x] Tab: the line moves right and becomes a point.

     Why: Tab makes a line a point under the title above it.

   - [ ] Shift + Tab

     Why: Shift + Tab makes a line a title, the other way.

   - [ ] Enter

     Why: Enter makes a new line at the same level.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-09/sims/outline-lab.html" poster="../../week-09/sims/outline-lab.png" title="Outline Lab: from an AI outline to slides" >}}

3. In **Outline Lab**, do the four tasks for Huda's talk *Going paperless*:
   the levels, the wrong number, the invented source and the long point.
   Which number was wrong?

   {{< record "The AI wrote … ; Huda's notes say …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI wrote **9,000** pages; Huda's notes say **6,500**. Compare every
   number with your own data, and delete the source that does not exist.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI outline names a report that no search finds. What do you do?

   - [x] Delete the line: the source does not exist.

     Why: An invented source is a hallucination.

   - [ ] Keep it: a source makes the talk look serious.

     Why: A source that does not exist is dishonest.

   - [ ] Make it smaller.

     Why: A wrong line stays wrong in a small font.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A picture for a slide

**The idea:** an **image prompt** has five parts: the **subject**, the
**style** (a flat illustration, a photo), the **colours** of your theme,
the **shape** (wide 16:9 next to the points) and "**no text** in the
picture". Check an AI picture closely: letters, hands and small details are
often wrong. No real people and no brands; write **alt text**, and the note
"AI-generated" under an AI picture. A **stock image** (Insert › Pictures ›
Stock Images) is often the better choice.

**Aim:** write an image prompt, and add a picture with alt text.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Write an image prompt for the slide *Sleep well* in the notes of that
   slide, with the five parts. Then insert a picture from **Insert ›
   Pictures › Stock Images** (search *sleep* or *bed*), make it smaller
   from a corner, and write its alt text.

   {{< record "My image prompt … ; my alt text …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good prompt, for example: *A flat illustration of a student asleep in
   bed, in soft blue and orange, wide 16:9, no text in the picture.* A good
   alt text says what the picture shows, for example "A student sleeps in a
   bed at night".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which shape fits a picture next to the points of a slide?

   - [x] wide 16:9

     Why: A wide picture fits next to the points.

   - [ ] tall 9:16

     Why: A tall picture is for a phone screen, not a slide.

   - [ ] any shape: PowerPoint stretches it

     Why: A stretched picture looks wrong: choose the shape in the prompt.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-09/sims/image-prompt-lab.html" poster="../../week-09/sims/image-prompt-lab.png" title="Image Prompt Lab: a picture for a slide" >}}

2. In **Image Prompt Lab**, build the prompt for Huda's slide, press
   **Generate**, write the alt text and the note, then try the prompt with
   words on a sign. What goes wrong?

   {{< record "With words on a sign: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The **letters are wrong**: AI pictures often draw wrong or strange
   letters. Ask for "no text in the picture", and write text on the slide
   instead.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which note goes under an AI picture on a slide?

   - [x] AI-generated

     Why: An honest note tells the audience how the picture was made.

   - [ ] the name of the AI company only

     Why: Say that it is AI-generated.

   - [ ] nothing

     Why: An AI picture needs an honest note.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · Check before you present

**The idea:** before the talk, five checks. **Facts and numbers:** compare
every number with your own data. **Sources:** open each one; delete one
that does not exist. **Your words:** write the speaker notes yourself.
**Few words:** 3–5 points of at most 8 words. **Honest:** a short note on
the last slide says what the AI did.

**Aim:** check the talk, and make it honest and yours.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Check your talk with the five checks. Write two or three sentences of
   speaker notes in your own words on one slide. Add a last slide with the
   note *Outline made with AI help and checked by me.*

   {{< record "One change after the checks … ; my note on the last slide …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer, for example: "I shortened a point of 11 words" or "I
   deleted a number that I could not check". The last slide says what the
   AI did. Save the file as `healthy-habits.pptx`.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which check finds each problem? Sort them.

   Facts and numbers
   :   The AI wrote 9,000 pages; your notes say 6,500.

       Why: Compare every number with your own data.

   Sources
   :   "Green Office Report 2021" cannot be found.

       Why: Open each source; delete one that does not exist.

   Few words
   :   A slide has five long sentences.

       Why: 3–5 points of at most 8 words.

   Honest
   :   Nobody knows that the outline came from AI.

       Why: A short note on the last slide says what the AI did.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-09/sims/slide-doctor.html" poster="../../week-09/sims/slide-doctor.png" title="Slide Doctor: fix the slide" kind="game" >}}

2. Play **Slide Doctor**: each slide of the Sunrise team has one problem.
   Choose the best fix. What is the fix for light grey text on light blue?

   {{< record "The fix for light grey on light blue: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Dark text on a light background**: a strong contrast that the back of
   the room can read.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The shop photo on a slide is tall and thin. What do you do?

   - [x] Resize it from a corner.

     Why: A corner keeps the shape of the picture.

   - [ ] Pull a side handle.

     Why: A side handle stretches the picture.

   - [ ] Delete the picture.

     Why: Fix the shape; the picture can stay.
   :::
